collected_dynamic_variables.pain_points: We lose calls after hours, callers hang up instead of leaving voicemail
collected_dynamic_variables.call_volume: About 15 calls a week go to voicemail

transcript:
User: Hi, I saw your ad about missed calls. We lose calls after hours and I'm curious how it works.
Agent: Got it, thanks for telling me that — a lot of people call us for exactly that after-hours gap.  

So when you close for the day and a call comes in at, say, 7 or 8pm, what actually happens to that caller right now — does it ring out, go to voicemail, or something else?
User: The calls go to voicemail after hours.
Agent: Gotcha, so after hours everything just drops into voicemail.  

Mhm, and do people actually leave messages for you, or do you feel like most of those callers just hang up and probably call someone else?
User: Yes, callers often hang up. About 15 calls a week go to voicemail.
Agent: Yeah, that adds up fast — 15 calls a week where many just disappear is a lot of missed business.  

So, to your question about how it works: our system picks up those after-hours calls right away, talks to the caller like a real receptionist, and either books the appointment, takes down the full message, or sends you a qualified lead instead of letting it sit in voicemail.  

What kind of business are you running, so I can explain it in your world instead of in general terms?
User: I run an auto repair shop in Austin, TX.
Agent: Nice, thanks for sharing that — auto repair is exactly one of the spots where this hurts the most, especially with after-hours and morning rush calls.  

Before I walk through how it would work for your shop specifically, has anyone ever actually shown you the math on what those 15 missed calls a week are costing you?
User: No, I haven't seen the exact math, but I know it impacts potential bookings and revenue.
Agent: Makes sense, most shop owners just feel it but never see the numbers.  

So, ballpark for your auto repair tickets — on average, what do you usually bring in from a typical job: more like $300, $600, or closer to $1,000?
User: On average, a typical job brings in about $450.
Agent: Got it, $450 per job is really helpful to know.  

Next piece of the puzzle: out of those 15 calls a week that hit voicemail, how many do you feel would actually book with you if someone picked up — maybe half, around 8, or more like 10–12?
User: About 60% would book if someone answered, so roughly 9 out of 15.
Agent: Right, so with your numbers, that’s roughly $17,500 a month in work tied to those missed calls — even saving a slice of that is meaningful.  

So… to actually see how this would plug into your shop and what those numbers look like with it turned on, we do a quick 20‑minute walkthrough — is later today or tomorrow better for you?
User: Tomorrow works better for me.
Agent: Perfect, we can set up a 20‑minute walkthrough with Jay tomorrow, no commitment — you just see it in action for your shop and then decide.  

Quick thing so I can lock this in for you: what’s your first name?
User: I'm Danny Reyes.
Agent: Nice to meet you, Danny.  

And what’s the name of your auto repair shop?
User: The name of my shop is Precision Auto Care.
Agent: Nice, Precision Auto Care — got it.  

So for tomorrow, we’ve got openings around late afternoon; I can get you in at either 5:00 or 5:45 Central — which one fits your day better?
User: 5:00 Central works for me. Please book it.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that for you.
Agent: Danny, you’re all set — you’re booked with Jay tomorrow at 5:00 Central for a 20-minute walkthrough. You’ll get an SMS confirmation in a moment with all the details, and you can reschedule from that link if something comes up. Is there anything else you need from me before we hop off?
